questions.prompt: MAX_DEPTH is 2. An agent at depth 2 calls the subagent tool. What happens?
options: The call gets an error result telling it to do the work directly
The call waits until a slot frees up
questions.explanation: The check is depth >= MAX_DEPTH, and 2 >= 2 is true, so the tool refuses with an error result the model can read.

questions.prompt: Why also put a sentence about the limit in the prompt, when the tool already refuses?
options: The tool check only runs in tests
The model would otherwise not see tool errors
So the model does not waste a step calling a tool that will refuse
The prompt sentence raises the limit by one
questions.explanation: A refused call still costs a model request. Telling the model in advance lets a well-behaved model do the work directly.

questions.prompt: Why must a child's depth be saved in its session file?
options: So a child resumed after a restart is not rebuilt at depth 0 and allowed to delegate like the top agent
So the parent can read it in its derived history
Because the model needs it to pick a tool
Because the depth decides the token budget
questions.explanation: If depth lived only in memory, a resumed child would start from 0 and the cap would no longer hold.
